proof:
# A Minkowski chain with every independent enlargement reserve locked
fiber enlargement. It is not a counterexample to OC and does not assert
that the family minimizes depth.

Let T=conv{(0,0),(1,0),(0,1)}, Q=[0,1]^2, and

    C=conv(({0} x T) union ({3} x Q)) subset R x R^2.

For j=0,1,2,3 its integer fiber is

    K_j=(1-j/3)T+(j/3)Q.

These are all its nonempty integer fibers, and C is a convex body.
For t in [0,1], direct Minkowski addition, or comparison of the five
support inequalities and vertices, gives

    K(t)=(1-t)T+tQ=[0,1]^2 intersect {x+y<=1+t}.

For 0<t<1 its vertices are (0,0),(1,0),(1,t),(t,1),(0,1).
At the endpoints the redundant vertices coincide or the diagonal facet
vanishes. Thus the facet normals of every K_j belong to

    N={-e_1,-e_2,e_1,e_2,e_1+e_2},

and both K_1 and K_2 have all five normals.

## Exact volumes and centroids

The removed corner triangle has area (1-t)^2/2 and centroid
((2+t)/3,(2+t)/3). Consequently, writing g(t)=(c(t),c(t)),

    v(t)=1-(1-t)^2/2,
    c(t)=[1/2-((1-t)^2/2)(2+t)/3]/v(t).

At the four integer fibers these give

    (v_0,v_1,v_2,v_3)=(1/2,7/9,17/18,1),
    (c_0,c_1,c_2,c_3)=(1/3,53/126,73/153,1/2).

Their total volume is M=29/9. Every fiber volume is at most 1<M/2.
The two same-parity centroid midpoint defects are nonzero:

    c_1-(c_0+c_2)/2=11/714,
    c_2-(c_1+c_3)/2=2/119.

In contrast, the support functions are exactly affine in j, so

    K_1=(K_0+K_2)/2,       K_2=(K_1+K_3)/2.        (1)

## Every independent monotone enlargement is impossible

Fix p in {0,1,2,3}. Suppose L_p is a compact convex superset of K_p,
all other fibers remain K_j, and this modified family is realized as
the integer fibers of some convex set. We prove L_p=K_p.

For p=0 use the first relation in (1), with target fiber 1. Actual
convexity requires (L_0+K_2)/2 subset K_1. For each facet normal u of
K_0, taking support functions and using (1) gives

    h_{L_0}(u)<=2h_{K_1}(u)-h_{K_2}(u)=h_{K_0}(u).

The facet inequalities of K_0 therefore contain L_0, proving equality.
Exactly the same argument works for p=2 with target 1 and source 0.
For p=1 use target 2 and source 3 in the second relation; for p=3 use
target 2 and source 1. In every case all facet normals of the source
are among the target's facet normals, and the support equality holds.
(The support argument itself does not require this latter containment.)
Thus every one of the four independent monotone enlargement reserves
is exactly its original fiber.

In fact support equality in every direction in (1) already proves the
claim directly: h_{L_p}<=h_{K_p} in every direction. The facet argument
makes explicit its finite polyhedral certificate.

## Dimension padding

For d>=2 replace each K_j by K_j x [0,1]^(d-2). The resulting convex
body is C x [0,1]^(d-2), its fiber volumes are unchanged, and its
centroids have the preceding first two coordinates followed by 1/2.
The exact Minkowski relations (1) remain valid in all d coordinates;
the same support proof locks every independently enlarged full fiber.

For n>=1 take the product in the integer coordinates with [0,1]^(n-1).
The base is {0,1,2,3} x {0,1}^(n-1), with k=2^n occupied parities.
Each binary copy retains both midpoint relations. They lock every
single-fiber enlargement, even if cross-copy constraints are ignored.
Total volume is 2^(n-1)29/9, so M/k=29/18>1 and no fiber is heavy at
the relevant threshold. Every copy has the displayed centroid defects.

The conclusion is limited but exact: positive midpoint centroid defect,
even with a complete lattice base and no heavy fiber, need not yield
ANY independent monotone fiber enlargement. A deformation argument for
such a family must change several fibers together, allow signed shape
changes, or employ a different mechanism.
